maria (eng-runtime): Heads-up — received a high-priority support escalation from DeltaCorp. They saw a sudden jump in p95/p99 for generation calls after yesterday's kernel rollout.

josh (support): DeltaCorp says p99 for requests with ~1200 token contexts went from ~600ms to ~1.8s. Started ~30m post-deploy. They included one request_id=delta-2026-03-14-11 and a curl to repro.

sam (eng-ml): Which runtime flags were changed in that deploy? Any attention/kernel toggles?
dev-bot: deploy 2026-03-14T10:42Z: runtime:kernel_heuristic=auto, flash_attention=on, compile_flags=[FA_OPTIM, ALIGN_WORKSPACE_FAST]

nina (perf): That matches what I saw in the build logs. We shipped an updated kernel selector that prefers FlashAttention for fp16 + seq_len>512.

alex (oncall): I tried to repro on staging with their payload. Baseline (pre-rollout binary) p95 ~520ms; after current binary, p95 ~1.5s and p99 ~2.1s for same seed.

maria (eng-runtime): FlashAttention is meant to be faster. Possible regressions: kernel tail latency, workspace reallocations, or a slow path when repetitive prefixes are present.

sam (eng-ml): Agreed. DeltaCorp mentioned repeated token prefixes in payload. Flash kernels sometimes take fallback paths if shapes trigger microkernel serialization. Will check.

josh (support): They also reported transient 429s during spikes. Probably backpressure from worker threads occupied by long-running flash kernels.

nina (perf): Preliminary kernel metrics: when we select fa_kernel_v3, median kernel time 140ms, p95 620ms, p99 1820ms. For sdpa_v2 on same card: median 160ms, p95 410ms, p99 560ms. FA tail looks terrible for some inputs.

sam (eng-ml): Could be allocator fragmentation at specific workspace sizes. FA requests sometimes need a large workspace that triggers internal cudaMalloc/cudaFree churn.

maria (eng-runtime): Immediate mitigations we can take: (A) Per-customer routing override to force SDPA kernels for DeltaCorp (B) Flip heuristic on canaries to prefer SDPA globally (C) Expose env var RDW_PREFERRED_KERNEL=sdpa for affected pools. Which should we do now?

alex (oncall): I'll apply the per-customer routing override to route their traffic to sdpa kernel variants only. Can do now on canary layer.

sam (eng-ml): I'll prepare a tiny runtime patch that adds a heuristic fallback: if FA kernel experiences >X ms during a warmup window, fallback to SDPA for that model instance. Also add a guard on workspace realloc frequency.

nina (perf): I'll collect nvtx traces and heap usage for the failing runs and generate flamegraphs. Need to capture a few of their real request payloads. Josh, can we get those?

josh (support): DeltaCorp shared 3 request payloads (repetitive prefix + long generation). Sending now. They confirmed their p99 dropped to ~540ms after Alex applied the override.

maria (eng-runtime): Good. Let's log an incident: RD-INC-5901. Sam, Nina — can you triage and open a vendor issue if we find a FlashAttention bug? Also add an alert: if kernel=flash_attention p99 > 1.3x baseline for >5m, trigger an automated route failover.
dev-bot: action created: RD-INC-5901 "flash_attention tail latency for long-context workloads" assigned to sam; due 2026-03-18

sam (eng-ml): Repro steps I'm using:
```
# repro script
python reproduce_latency.py --model rwd-13b-qlora --input delta_payload.txt --gen-tokens 1024 --batch 1
# compare kernels
RDW_PREFERRED_KERNEL=flash python reproduce_latency.py ...
RDW_PREFERRED_KERNEL=sdpa python reproduce_latency.py ...

# collect nvprof traces
NVTX_CAPTURE=1 python reproduce_latency.py ...
```
I consistently see sdpa p99 ~560ms, flash p99 ~1.6-2.0s with same RNG.

nina (perf): NVTX shows FA launches a series of tiny microkernels with grid dims that lead to sequential execution on SMs for certain head/seq shapes. Also workspace allocator shows fragmentation spikes around 1.1 GiB leading to fallback allocations.

sam (eng-ml): Proposed short-term plan:
- Apply routing override for DeltaCorp (done)
- Roll back flash_attention heuristic on 20% of nodes (canary rollback)
- Ship runtime flag --fa-fallback-ms=700 that triggers per-model fallback to sdpa if observed kernel time exceeds threshold during warmup.

maria (eng-runtime): Sounds right. Also update runbook: when p99 doubles after kernel change, do immediate per-customer override and enable canary rollback. Add note about checking workspace fragmentation metrics.

alex (oncall): I rolled the routing override at 2026-03-14T12:07Z. DeltaCorp confirmed p99 back to ~560ms within 6 minutes. They said their product is unblocked but want root cause and timeline for full fix.

josh (support): Customer thanked us and asked for ETA. We told them we'll follow up with vendor outreach if necessary and estimate 3-7 days pending root cause.

sam (eng-ml): I opened PR #4052 with the warmup fallback and allocator guard. It's a small change behind a feature gate: FA_FALLBACK_ENABLED=true + FA_FALLBACK_MS=700. Low-risk, needs quick review.

nina (perf): For mid-term: we should rebuild FlashAttention with improved workspace alignment and test different allocator strategies. Also add a synthetic test that covers repeated-token prefixes and long generation to catch regressions in CI.

maria (eng-runtime): Agreed. Ops: add an automated dashboard tile showing kernel-specific p50/p95/p99 and workspace alloc churn, and a thresholded alert. Support: update KB entry for kernel regressions and note the per-customer override workflow.

alex (oncall): Reviewing PR now. If merged, we can canary the fallback on 10% nodes and monitor. We'll only do wide rollout once vendor/allocator fixes are in or until metrics are green for 48h.

josh (support): I'll draft the postmortem placeholder and keep DeltaCorp in the loop. They asked for a note on whether this could affect other customers — we should proactively scan high-context models for similar regressions.

nina (perf): I'll run a quick cluster scan overnight for models with seq_len>512 and flash_attention selected and surface anomalies.

sam (eng-ml): Next steps assigned: PR review (alex), NVTX artifacts + vendor bug (nina), runtime patch + canary (sam), routing override remains until canary stable (maria).

maria (eng-runtime): Thanks. Reopen this thread with any new reproductions or if DeltaCorp shares more traces. If anyone finds a specific head/seq shape that deterministically causes serialization, paste it here. :eyes:
